```{r}
# Data Setup - Converting to Time Series
library(fpp2)
library(forecast)

TOTALNSA <- read.csv("TOTALNSA.csv")

TOTALNSA$observation_date <- as.Date(
  TOTALNSA$observation_date,
  format = "%m/%d/%Y")

TOTALNSA_ts <- ts(
  TOTALNSA$TOTALNSA,
  start = c(1976, 1),
  frequency = 12)

plot(TOTALNSA_ts)

mean_forecast <- meanf(TOTALNSA_ts,12)
naive_forecast <- naive(TOTALNSA_ts,12)
rwf_forecast <- rwf(TOTALNSA_ts,12, drift = TRUE)
snaive_forecast <- snaive(TOTALNSA_ts,12)
ets_forecast <- forecast(ets(TOTALNSA_ts),12)
HW_forecast <- forecast(HoltWinters(TOTALNSA_ts),12)

auto_fit <- auto.arima(
  TOTALNSA_ts,
  trace = TRUE,
  stepwise = FALSE)

ARIMA_forecast <- forecast(
  auto_fit,
  h = 5,
  level = c(95))

plot(HW_forecast,
     main = "Holt-Winters Forecast",
     xlab = "Year",
     ylab = "TOTALNSA",
     xlim = c(2000, 2027))

plot(TOTALNSA_ts,
     main = "TOTALNSA Forecast Comparison",
     xlab = "Year",
     ylab = "TOTALNSA",
     xlim = c(2000, 2027))
lines(mean_forecast$mean, col="pink",lwd = 2)
lines(naive_forecast$mean, col="blue",lwd = 2)
lines(rwf_forecast$mean, col="green",lwd = 2)
lines(snaive_forecast$mean, col="orange",lwd = 2)
lines(ets_forecast$mean, col="purple", lwd = 2)
lines(HW_forecast$mean, col="darkgreen", lwd = 2)
lines(ARIMA_forecast$mean, col="red", lwd = 2)

# Legend
legend("bottomleft",
       legend = c("Mean",
                  "Naive",
                  "Random Walk with Drift",
                  "Seasonal Naive",
                  "ETS",
                  "Holt-Winters",
                  "ARIMA"),
       col = c("pink", "blue", "green",
               "orange", "purple",
               "darkgreen", "red"),
       lty = 1,
       lwd = 2,
       cex = 0.6,
       bty = "n")


# MAE Comparison - Actual Assignment Results
MAE_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Mean",
    "Naive",
    "Random Walk",
    "Seasonal Naive",
    "ETS",
    "Holt-Winters",
    "ARIMA"),
  MAE = c(
    1.2767900,
    0.4214444,
    0.4074639,
    0.7665556,
    0.4505718,
    0.4066513,
    0.4150615))

# Highlight model with lowest MAE
bar_colors <- rep("steelblue", 7)
bar_colors[which.min(MAE_comparison$MAE)] <- "darkgreen"

# Create Bar Chart
bars <- barplot(
  MAE_comparison$MAE,
  names.arg = MAE_comparison$Model,
  main = "MAE Comparison Across Forecasting Models",
  ylab = "Mean Absolute Error (MAE)",
  col = bar_colors,
  las = 2,
  cex.names = 0.6,
  ylim = c(0, max(MAE_comparison$MAE) * 1.2))

# Display actual MAE above each bar
text(
  x = bars,
  y = MAE_comparison$MAE,
  labels = sprintf("%.4f", MAE_comparison$MAE),
  pos = 3,
  cex = 0.85,
  col = "black")

# Print MAE comparison
print(MAE_comparison)
```
